title: JUnit 5's provider extension makes each interaction a test of its own: a verified one passes, a failed one fails with its mismatches.
why: behavioural spec 'verify': the engine calls each handler the verifier declared during the run, and a failed run fails, naming each result whose status is 'failed'. The JVM style guide, 'Provider test-framework integration' (ADR 0056 decision 3): each interaction result is a dynamic test named '<consumer>: <description>'; 'verified' passes, and anything else fails, with the result's mismatches or error.
note: JUnit 5 alone has this spelling: a framework with dynamic tests, and the extension the JVM SDK ships for it. The other frameworks verify a provider in one test (framework/provider-verifies-in-a-test).
